messages:
maria: quick signal after the FA v3 rollout on staging — we're seeing throughput drop ~10-15% for mid-length (256-512) sequences on A100s. anyone else see this?
chris: saw it too on the nightly perf dash. p50 token time up ~12% on the chat workload.
sam: can you paste the specific run id / model + config?
maria: run id 2026-03-fa3-07, model `redwood-mini-7B` fp16, batch=8, seq=384. kernels: flashattn_v3 preferred, fallback to fa_v2 in some cases.
chris: thanks. initial hypothesis: kernel selection heuristic is favoring v3 kernels that have higher kernel-launch overhead for mid sequences. v3 shines on long seqs and BF16 path.
jing: also noticed memory allocator fragmentation on long lived pods — workspace allocation patterns changed with v3. small-ish extra workspace per layer adds up and pushes us into different alloc paths.
maria: here's a short log snippet from the failing run:
```
[perf] model=redwood-mini-7B seq=384 batch=8 tokens/s=1120 p50=28ms p90=72ms kernel=flashattn_v3 launch_us=8 compute_us=70
[perf] baseline model=... tokens/s=1260 p50=25ms p90=68ms kernel=flashattn_v2 launch_us=3 compute_us=60
```
chris: launch_us diff seems suspicious (8 vs 3). that suggests kernel warmup / different kernel binary selection. do we fallback to a generic kernel when shapes misalign?
sam: current heuristic: choose kernel by (seq, batch, dtype, model_arch) with some thresholds. if workspace reservation fails we fallback to fa_v2. but we also have per-device kernel list ordering.
ops-bot: FYI deploy bot: canary rollout at 2005001000 -> 2005001200 completed on staging clusters.
maria: is the workspace rounding different in v3? maybe we allocate bigger alignment causing fragmentation. jing, can you dump allocator telemetry?
jing: will do. one immediate thought: v3 uses tiled workspace sizes that round up to 256B boundaries and sometimes allocate an extra chunk per head for fwd/back. that could push total workspace *over* our allocator size class and cause a new cudaMalloc event.
chris: other angle: nvprims / kernel launch configuration. v3 kernels use more dynamic shared memory which affects occupancy. on some SM configs the occupancy drop increases compute_us.
sam: actionable list I propose:
- add a microbenchmark that runs seq in [64,128,256,384,512,768,1024] and logs `launch_us` and `compute_us` per kernel variant
- add workspace allocation telemetry (size class, fragmentation events, #cudaMallocs) per request
- tweak kernel selection to bias v3 for seq>=768 and v2 for 64-512 until we validate
- revert canary if p95 or tokens/s regresses >5%
maria: +1. also add an experiment toggling `prefer_bf16` to false; v3 may be optimized for bf16 on some cards. our test was fp16.
chris: pinging @jing and @sam for PRs. I'll prepare a short RFC-ish note describing the interim selector change so we can roll it to prod quickly.
jing: allocator dump shows these during the run:
```
alloc_trace: [size=2.1MB class=2MB -> fragmentation=512KB], [size=1.8MB class=2MB -> ok], cuda_mallocs=12 during init phase
workspace_reserved_total=128MB expected, actual_committed=192MB
```
jing: seems we crossed the reservation threshold and triggered extra vm mappings forcing device-level contention.
maria: interesting — that could explain p90 tail. any quick config to reduce per-layer workspace?
sam: we can change workspace policy: `prefer_reuse = true` (more aggressive reuse), `max_workspace_per_gpu=150MB` on staging to see impact. also reduce default max_heads_tile in v3 to drop extra per-head workspace.
chris: can we add a fallback policy that chooses kernel by estimated end-to-end cost: cost = launch_us + compute_us * (seq / base_seq) + penalty_if_new_malloc? we have telemetry to estimate those components.
jing: yes. we can approximate penalty_if_new_malloc from recent runs. it's crude but better than pure rule-based.
maria: timeline: can we have the microbench + telemetry in staging by EOD?
sam: I'll open the microbench PR now and wire telemetry events. aiming for a deploy in 4 hours.
chris: I'll draft the selector patch as a canary toggle. it will default to previous behavior but allow override via `kernel_selector_lane` in model config.
maria: when you push, drop a link here. I'll run the regression harness. if tokens/s recovers we can roll forward.
ci-deploy-bot: CI: microbench tests added by @sam passed (12/12), build artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/arch/2005/fa3-microbench/
sam: PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/4823 — microbench + telemetry.
chris: PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/4824 — selector toggle + simple cost estimator.
jing: changed allocator defaults on staging pool `staging-fa3` to `max_workspace_per_gpu=150MB prefer_reuse=true`. will monitor.
maria: after the change, quick rerun shows tokens/s back to ~1240 for seq=384 batch=8. still slightly below baseline but within noise. p50 improved to 26ms.
sam: that'll do for now. longer term we should:
- expand microbench CI matrix to more cards (H100, A10)
- add per-kernel occupancy telemetry (smem, regs)
- consider moving workspace allocator to pooled mmap to avoid cross-request fragmentation
chris: agree. I'll schedule a follow-up RFC on allocator refactor.
maria: thanks all. tagging this thread for postmortem notes. will update the rollout doc depending on CI runs. :white_check_mark:
